claims.text: Initially solid, single-phase Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles contain equiatomic proportions of the five elements.
Local compositional fluctuations in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles enhance heterogeneous surface segregation.
Local compositional fluctuations in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles accelerate surface diffusion.
Enhanced segregation and surface diffusion lower the effective premelting-to-melting temperature range relative to compositionally uniform monometallic or bimetallic nanoparticles.
Surface elemental segregation patterns and local compositional inhomogeneities emerge during heating.
Minor local fluctuations in a multielement composition produce differential surface-energy effects.
Differential surface-energy effects promote accelerated, heterogeneous atomic diffusion and selective elemental segregation.
Accelerated diffusion and selective segregation destabilize the nanoparticle surface at lower temperatures.
Surface destabilization advances the onset of premelting relative to simpler monometallic or bimetallic systems.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles will exhibit surface disordering at a lower temperature than the baseline particles.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles will exhibit greater surface atomic diffusion than the baseline particles.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles will exhibit detectable elemental segregation at lower temperatures than the baseline particles.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles will undergo a more gradual and earlier premelting-to-melting transition than the baseline particles.
Uniform monometallic or simple bimetallic baseline nanoparticles have slower surface-diffusion kinetics than the HEA nanoparticles.
The proposed mechanism is limited to sub-10 nm, homogeneous solid-solution particles subjected to moderate heating rates under ultrahigh vacuum.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to larger particles, different alloy systems, or drastically different heating protocols.
The relative contributions of compositional fluctuations and size-related surface-energy effects are uncertain.
Absence of a statistically significant earlier disordering onset, enhanced surface diffusion, or selective segregation relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
